name: MOTIVE
aliases: Male Overactive Bladder Treatment in Veterans
question: In men with persistent overactive bladder symptoms after alpha-blocker treatment, is behavioral therapy equivalent to adding oxybutynin extended release for daily voiding frequency?

design.blinding: Blinded diary scoring; participant and clinician blinding not reported

arms.label: Behavioral therapy added to alpha-blocker treatment
oxybutynin extended release added to alpha-blocker treatment

design.population: Men aged 42–88 years screened for low uroflow and elevated postvoid residual who still had urgency and more than eight daily voids after a four-week alpha-blocker run-in.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, Participants and Design, pp 2210–2211; Results, p 2211

verdictNote: Posttreatment daily voiding frequency met the prespecified ±15% equivalence margin.
takeaway: In 143 men with persistent overactive bladder symptoms after alpha-blocker treatment, eight weeks of behavioral therapy and titrated oxybutynin extended release produced equivalent posttreatment daily voiding frequency (9.1 versus 9.5 voids/day among 124 completers; adjusted equivalence P = .001).

reports.label: Primary equivalence report
reports.citation: Burgio KL, Goode PS, Johnson TM, et al. "Behavioral Versus Drug Treatment for Overactive Bladder in Men: The Male Overactive Bladder Treatment in Veterans (MOTIVE) Trial." *J Am Geriatr Soc.* 2011;59(12):2209-2216. doi:10.1111/j.1532-5415.2011.03724.x
reports.followUp: Eight weeks of randomized treatment after a four-week alpha-blocker run-in
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, Design and Outcome Assessment, pp 2210–2211

results.measure: Mean voids per 24 hours at eight weeks among completers (behavioral n = 64; drug n = 60); baseline-adjusted TOST equivalence margin ±15% of drug-group posttreatment mean
results.note: Unadjusted completer TOST P = .006; last-observation-carried-forward intention-to-treat TOST P = .003; baseline-adjusted LOCF P < .001. No confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Power Analysis and Data Analysis, p 2211; Results, p 2212; Table 2, p 2213

results.measure: Mean change in nightly episodes at eight weeks among completers (behavioral n = 64; drug n = 60)

values.exp: 2.23 at baseline, 1.53 at eight weeks; change −0.70 episodes/night (n = 64)
values.ctl: 2.30 at baseline, 1.96 at eight weeks; change −0.32 episodes/night (n = 60)

results.measure: Mean change in maximum urgency score at eight weeks among assessed completers (behavioral n = 61; drug n = 60)

values.exp: 2.42 at baseline, 2.30 at eight weeks; change −0.12 (n = 61)
values.ctl: 2.37 at baseline, 1.93 at eight weeks; change −0.44 (n = 60)

harms.label: Somewhat or extremely bothersome side effects at eight weeks

values.exp: 12.6% (Table 3 behavioral respondents n = 63; item denominator not specified)
values.ctl: 28.8% (Table 3 drug respondents n = 60; item denominator not specified)

harms.note: Respondent percentages are reported without item-level numerator or denominator; P = .01 for the ordinal side-effect rating comparison.
harms.locator: Full text, Results, Patient Global Ratings, p 2212; Table 3, p 2214

delivery.label: Behavioral treatment
delivery.value: Four nurse-practitioner clinic visits over eight weeks; pelvic floor contractions taught with anal-palpation feedback, usually 15 exercises three times daily, plus urge suppression, delayed voiding and nocturnal fluid restriction after 6 p.m.; added after a four-week alpha-blocker run-in.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Intervention and Behavioral Treatment, p 2210

delivery.label: Drug treatment
delivery.value: Four clinic visits over eight weeks; oxybutynin extended release started at 10 mg/day and titrated to 5–30 mg/day; dose reduced to 5 mg if postvoid residual exceeded 150 mL; added after a four-week alpha-blocker run-in.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Intervention and Drug Therapy, pp 2210–2211

delivery.label: Treatment completion and final oxybutynin dose

values.ctl: 60/70 completed treatment and posttreatment assessment; at posttreatment 9 took 5 mg, 25 took 10 mg, 8 took 15 mg, 4 took 20 mg, 2 took 30 mg, and 12 reported no current drug use

delivery.locator: Full text, Figure 1 and Results, p 2212

reports.label: Nocturia analysis
reports.citation: Johnson TM 2nd, Markland AD, Goode PS, et al. "Efficacy of Adding Behavioural Treatment or Antimuscarinic Drug Therapy to α-Blocker Therapy in Men with Nocturia." *BJU Int.* 2013;112(1):100-108. doi:10.1111/j.1464-410X.2012.11736.x
reports.followUp: Nocturia analysis at eight weeks after randomization

results.endpoint: Nocturia in men with at least one baseline nightly episode
results.measure: Mean change in nightly episodes at eight weeks among 127 randomized men with baseline nocturia ≥1/night (behavioral n = 64; drug n = 63); missing posttreatment values carried forward

values.exp: 2.50 at baseline, 1.52 at eight weeks; mean change −0.97 episodes/night (n = 64)
values.ctl: 2.31 at baseline, 1.75 at eight weeks; mean change −0.56 episodes/night (n = 63)

results.note: Between-group P value compares mean changes; the paper states no prespecified alpha or confidence interval.
results.locator: Full text, Outcome Assessment and Data Analysis, pp 102–103; Table 2, p 104

results.endpoint: Nocturia in men with at least two baseline nightly episodes
results.measure: Mean change in nightly episodes at eight weeks among 76 randomized men with baseline nocturia ≥2/night (behavioral n = 38; drug n = 38); missing posttreatment values carried forward

values.exp: 3.23 at baseline, 1.97 at eight weeks; mean change −1.26 episodes/night (n = 38)
values.ctl: 2.89 at baseline, 2.28 at eight weeks; mean change −0.61 episodes/night (n = 38)

results.note: Between-group P value compares mean changes; the paper states no prespecified alpha or confidence interval.
results.locator: Full text, Figure 1, p 101; Data Analysis, p 103; Table 3, p 104

values.exp: Self-rated pelvic floor exercise adherence 63% of prescribed exercises; adherence-report denominator not stated
values.ctl: Mean pill-count adherence 96% of prescribed oxybutynin; adherence-report denominator not stated
